title: Numbers, age & quantities
goal: Count things and people, ask 'how many / how much', give your age and phone number, and use ordinals 1st–10th.
intro:
Nepali numbers from 1 to 100 are all slightly irregular — 23 is तेइस, 33 तेत्तीस, 43 त्रिचालीस — so learn them from the **numbers chart** in small batches (1–20 first, then the tens, then fill in). You'll also see Devanagari digits ०१२३४५६७८९ everywhere in Nepal, from prices to bus numbers.

In this unit you'll learn how to use numbers in sentences: Nepali uses little **counter words** — वटा for things and जना for people — between the number and the noun.

vocab.en: how much; how many; how (+ adjective)
vocab.note: Also used for prices and phone numbers: नम्बर कति हो? and in exclamations: कति राम्रो! 'how nice!'
दुईवटा, तीनवटा… Also pronounced/spelled ओटा: दुईओटा.
f एउटी euṭi (with women/girls). Colloquially often 'yauṭā'.
एक जना, दुई जना, कति जना?
Colloquially बर्ष/बरस. 'X years old' = X वर्षको.
यो साल 'this year', अर्को साल 'next year'.
From 5th on, add -औँ to the number.
धेरै राम्रो 'very good', धेरै मान्छे 'lots of people'.
English loan; the native word संख्या is formal.
Eggs and bananas are sold by the dozen: एक दर्जन केरा.
एक पटक 'once', पहिलो पटक 'the first time'. Colloquially also चोटि choṭi.
Ground floor is भुइँ तला bhuiṃ talā.

phrases.en: How old are you? (lit. how many years old have you become?)

phrases.native: नेपाल आएको यो मेरो पहिलो पटक हो।
phrases.roman: Nepāl āeko yo mero pahilo paṭak ho.
phrases.en: This is my first time in Nepal.
My room is on the third floor.

grammar.title: Counting with वटा and जना
grammar.body:
When you count things, put a **counter word** between the number and the noun:

**things/animals**: number + **वटा** — दुई**वटा** किताब 'two books', पाँच**वटा** कुकुर 'five dogs'.
**people**: number + **जना** — तीन **जना** साथी 'three friends'.

'One thing' is the special word **एउटा** (एउटी for a woman or girl). It also works like English 'a/an': एउटा कुरा 'a thing'. For one person you can say एक जना or एउटा मान्छे.

The noun stays **singular** after a number — no -हरू needed. With big round numbers, measures and money the counter is usually left out: सय रुपैयाँ '100 rupees', दुई किलो '2 kilos', तीन दिन '3 days'.

Big numbers: **सय** 100, **हजार** 1,000, **लाख** 100,000, **करोड** 10 million. Nepal writes them grouped the South Asian way: १,००,००० = one lakh.

examples.en: There are twenty students in the class.
This is one and a half lakh (150,000) rupees.

grammar.title: Asking 'how much / how many'
grammar.body:
**कति** asks about amount, number or price. Add the counter to be precise: **कतिवटा** 'how many (things)', **कति जना** 'how many (people)'. कति also asks for phone numbers and room numbers, where English uses 'what': नम्बर कति हो?

The answer usually just replaces कति with the number.

examples.en: How many eggs do you need?
How many people are in your class?

grammar.title: Age and ordinals
grammar.body:
To give your age, say literally 'I have become X years-of': **म तीस वर्षको भएँ** 'I'm thirty'. The question is **कति वर्षको हुनुभयो?** (polite) or **कति वर्षको भयौ?** (to a child/friend). You can also say मेरो उमेर तीस वर्ष हो 'my age is 30'.

**Ordinals**: पहिलो 1st, दोस्रो 2nd, तेस्रो 3rd, चौथो 4th — then add **-औँ** to the number: पाँचौँ 5th, छैटौँ 6th (irregular), सातौँ, आठौँ, नवौँ, दसौँ, एघारौँ, बीसौँ… Like other -ओ adjectives, पहिलो/दोस्रो/तेस्रो/चौथो change to -ई for females (पहिली छोरी 'first daughter').

examples.en: He came first in the class.

dialogue.title: At the guesthouse
dialogue.setting: Tom arrives at a family guesthouse in Pokhara with his wife and daughter. The owner greets them at reception.

lines.speaker: Owner
lines.en: Hello! How many of you are there?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: हामी तीन जना छौँ — दुई जना ठूला मान्छे र एउटी सानी छोरी।
lines.roman: hāmi tin janā chhauṃ — dui janā ṭhulā mānchhe ra euṭi sāni chhori.
lines.en: We're three — two adults and our little daughter.

lines.speaker: Owner
lines.en: How old is the little one?

lines.speaker: Owner
lines.en: OK. How many nights will you stay?

lines.speaker: Owner
lines.native: तपाईंको कोठा नम्बर एक सय बाह्र हो, दोस्रो तलामा।
lines.roman: tapāiṃko koṭhā nambar ek saya bāhra ho, dosro talāmā.
lines.en: Your room is number 112, on the second floor.

lines.speaker: Owner
lines.native: एक रातको अढाई हजार, जम्मा साढे सात हजार।
lines.roman: ek rātko aḍhāi hajār, jammā sāḍhe sāt hajār.
lines.en: Two and a half thousand a night, seven and a half thousand in total.

culture: Nepal uses its own calendar, the **Bikram Sambat** (विक्रम संवत्), which runs about 56 years and 8 months ahead of the Western one — so many Nepalis will tell you their age or birth year in both systems. Devanagari digits appear on number plates, bus routes and price tags, so it pays to read them fluently. When giving money as a gift (at weddings, Dashain or to priests) Nepalis add one rupee to make an 'unfinished', auspicious odd sum: रु. १०१, ५०१, १००१. Little girls are affectionately called **नानी** and little boys **बाबु**.

tip.title: Counter words: वटा and जना
tip.body:
- Put a counter between the number and the noun: things take **वटा** (दुई**वटा** झोला), people take **जना** (तीन **जना** साथी).
- 'One thing' / 'a' is **एउटा** (**एउटी** for a woman or girl).
- The noun stays singular after a number, and measures drop the counter: एक दर्जन अण्डा, सय रुपैयाँ.
tip.pattern: number + वटा + thing  ·  number + जना + person

sentences.en: There are five of us.
Where are my two bags?
Three teas, please.
There are two foreigners here.
I have one son.
She has a daughter.
It's just the two of us.
A dozen eggs, please.
Just count the bags, will you.

tip.title: कति: how much, how many
tip.body:
- **कति** asks about amount, number or price: यो कति हो? 'How much is this?'
- Add the counter: **कतिवटा** 'how many (things)', **कति जना** 'how many (people)'.
- Phone and room numbers use कति too: नम्बर **कति** हो?
- The answer just replaces कति with the number.

sentences.en: How much is this bag?
What's your phone number? (to a friend)
How many teas would you like?
How many brothers do you have?
How many rupees is that altogether?
How much is a dozen eggs?
Three hundred rupees altogether.
I need two.
How nice!

tip.title: Age and 'sixth, seventh…'
tip.body:
- Age is 'I have become X years-of': म तीस वर्षको **भएँ**. Ask तपाईं कति वर्षको **हुनुभयो**? (polite) or तिमी कति वर्षको **भयौ**? (friend, child).
- For a girl or woman: वर्ष**की**.
- Ordinals from 5th on add **-औँ**: सात → **सातौँ**, नौ → **नवौँ**, दस → **दसौँ**; 6th is **छैटौँ**.
tip.pattern: म + X + वर्षको + भएँ  ·  सात → सातौँ

sentences.en: How old are you? (to a boy or a friend)
I'm thirty.
My daughter is ten.
How old is your father?

sentences.native: यो साल मेरो छोरा आठ वर्षको भयो।
sentences.roman: yo sāl mero chhorā āṭh barsako bhayo.
sentences.en: My son turned eight this year.
I'm twenty. (lit. my age is twenty years)
My son is in class seven.
My younger sister is in class nine.

sentences.native: तिम्रो भाइ कुन कक्षामा पढ्छ? छैटौँ कि आठौँ?
sentences.roman: timro bhāi kun kakchhāmā paḍhchha? chhaiṭauṃ ki āṭhauṃ?
sentences.en: What class is your brother in? Six or eight?

sentences.native: यो साल ऊ दसौँ कक्षामा छ।
sentences.roman: yo sāl u dasauṃ kakchhāmā chha.
sentences.en: This year he's in class ten.

lessons.title: First time, third floor

tip.title: First, second, third…
tip.body:
- The first four are special: **पहिलो**, **दोस्रो**, **तेस्रो**, **चौथो**; then **पाँचौँ**, छैटौँ, सातौँ…
- **पटक** is 'time, occasion': पहिलो पटक 'the first time', एक पटक 'once', दुई पटक 'twice'.
- Floors: तेस्रो **तलामा** 'on the third floor'.

new: नेपाल आएको यो मेरो पहिलो पटक हो।

sentences.native: काठमाडौं आएको यो मेरो तेस्रो पटक हो।
sentences.roman: Kāṭhmāḍauṃ āeko yo mero tesro paṭak ho.
sentences.en: This is my third time in Kathmandu.

sentences.native: तपाईं नेपाल पहिलो पटक आउनुभएको हो?
sentences.roman: tapāiṃ Nepāl pahilo paṭak āunubhaeko ho?
sentences.en: Is this your first time in Nepal?
Our room is on the fourth floor.
Didi's room is on the fifth floor.
This is my second son.
Please say it once more.
Which floor is your room on?
It's on the second floor.
I didn't understand the first time.

tip.title: Amounts
tip.body:
- **धेरै** = 'a lot, many' and also 'very' before an adjective: धेरै राम्रो.
- **थोरै** = 'few, not much'; **अलिकति** = 'a little bit (of)', handy when someone is serving you.
- Halves: **आधा** ½, **डेढ** 1½, **अढाई** 2½: डेढ सय = 150, अढाई सय = 250.

sentences.en: It's very nice!
Just a little tea, please.
Just give me half, please.
There are lots of people here.
There are only a few students in the class.
It comes to 150 rupees altogether.
250 rupees, please.
I only speak a little Nepali.
Thanks a lot, brother!
